newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's Mubarak goes to Syria for talks with Assad.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Mubarak goes to Syria for talks with Assad.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak left for Syria on Tuesday on a previously unannounced visit and was expected to hold talks with President Hafez al-Assad, airport sources said.

His trip took place a day after Israel put the brakes on a plan to build a new Jewish enclave in Arab East Jerusalem and agreed to resume talks with the PLO on meeting commitments made under their interim peace deals.

Israel's Interior Ministry suspended a permit granted to a U.S. Jewish land baron to build 70 Jewish homes in an Arab neighbourhood until an appeal by two left-wing Jerusalem city council members had been heard.

Tuesday's edition of the Egyptian government daily al-Ahram newspaper said Mubarak sent a message to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday sounding a warning of the dangers to peace if Israel went ahead with plans to build the settlement.
Egypt in 1979 became the first Arab country to sign a peace treaty with Israel and has often mediated in peace talks between the Jewish state and its Arab neighbours.
